mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO rises > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines > 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month and the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 4%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters.
